units.title: 营谋·谋事五忌：谋事在人营求不一皆物交物而成，故六冲则不交、合而冲则将交而散、应空散则彼心不附、世空散则我意先慵、官鬼失而谋无主；唯世应破绝犹得其半（破绝有形空散无迹）

rule.yi: 谋事在人，营求的办法不一，都是物与物相交才成。所以六冲就交不到一起；合处逢冲，就将要交合却又（此处疑脱一字，当是「散」）；应空、散，对方的心就不依附；世空、散，我自己的意思先懒了；只有世应破、绝，还能得到一半；官鬼失去，谋事就没有主。这是五种忌。
rule.en: Scheming rests with men; the ways of seeking are not one, and all of them are accomplished by one thing meeting another. So with a six-clash they do not meet; with a combination clashed, they are about to join and then (a character seems lost here, presumably 'come apart'); with the Other Void or scattered, his heart does not attach to me; with the Self Void or scattered, my own will first turns slack; only with the Self and the Other broken or extinct is half still obtained; with Pressure lost, the scheme has no master. These are the five taboos.

zh: 夫谋事在人，营求不一，皆物交物而成也。
故六冲则不交，
合而冲，则将交而，
应空散，则彼心不附，
世空散，则我意先慵，
唯世应破绝，犹得其半，
官鬼失而谋无主，此五者之忌也。
yi: 谋事在人，营求的办法不一，都是物与物相交才成。
所以六冲就交不到一起；
合处逢冲，就将要交合却又（此处疑脱一字，当是「散」）；
应空、散，对方的心就不依附；
世空、散，我自己的意思先懒了；
只有世应破、绝，还能得到一半；
官鬼失去，谋事就没有主，这是五种忌。
en: Scheming rests with men; the ways of seeking are not one, and all of them are accomplished by one thing meeting another.
So with a six-clash they do not meet;
with a combination clashed, they are about to join and then (a character seems lost here, presumably 'come apart');
with the Other Void or scattered, his heart does not attach to me;
with the Self Void or scattered, my own will first turns slack;
only with the Self and the Other broken or extinct is half still obtained;
with Pressure lost, the scheme has no master. These are the five taboos.

zh: 破绝有形，空散无迹。
yi: 破、绝是有形的，空、散是没影的。
en: Broken and extinct have a form; Void and scattered leave no trace.

zh: 内附嘱托
yi: 本章里面附有嘱托一类的占问。
en: This chapter has attached to it divinations about entrusting a matter to another.

note.yi: 「谋事在人」是谋事要靠人去做，「营求」是经营求取，「物交物」是事物和事物相交、两边凑到一起才成。「六冲则不交」是六冲（散）就凑不到一起；「合而冲」是合处逢冲（见 YM.07 注）。「则将交而」后面原文疑脱一字，当是「散」，按文意译作「将要交合却又散开」。「应空散则彼心不附」是应是对方，应空、散就是对方没有心；「世空散则我意先慵」是世是自己，世空、散就是自己先懒了。「世应破绝，犹得其半」：破、绝是有形的，力量残存，所以还能成一半；空、散是没影的，所以是忌。「官鬼失而谋无主」是官鬼是谋事的主，没有它事无主持（见 YM.88）。五忌就是：六冲、合冲、应空散、世空散、官鬼失。这一章是营谋（谋求一件事）与嘱托（托人办事），和易隐谋望占（YY.82–88）、易林补遗谋望成事（EL.103 起）取同一类，章首「内附嘱托」就是嘱托也在这里。
note.en: 'Moushi zai ren' is that scheming has to be done by men, 'yingqiu' is managing and seeking, and 'wu jiao wu' is one thing meeting another, so that the two sides come together and it succeeds. 'With a six-clash they do not meet' is that a six-clash (scattering) cannot bring them together; 'a combination clashed' is a combination meeting a clash (see the note to YM.07). Below 'ze jiang jiao er' the original seems to lack a character, presumably 'san', scatter, and by the sense it is translated 'about to join and then comes apart'. 'The Other Void or scattered, his heart does not attach to me' is that the Other is the other side, and the Other Void or scattered means he has no heart for it; 'the Self Void or scattered, my own will first turns slack' is that the Self is myself, and the Self Void or scattered means I am the first to go slack. 'The Self and the Other broken or extinct, half is still obtained': broken and extinct have a form, some force remains, so half can still be had; Void and scattered leave no trace, so they are taboo. 'Pressure lost, the scheme has no master' is that Pressure is the master of a scheme, and without it the matter has no one to run it (see YM.88). The five taboos are: a six-clash, a combination clashed, the Other Void or scattered, the Self Void or scattered, and Pressure lost. This chapter is about scheming (seeking something) and entrusting (asking someone to act for one), of a kind with the Yi Yin on scheming and hope (YY.82-88) and the Yilin Buyi on accomplishing a scheme (from EL.103); 'attached: entrusting' at the head of the chapter means entrusting is treated here too.

units.title: 营谋·成否与吉凶：自力可成莫观其应、因人成事莫观其世；止问成否但忌空冲、兼问吉凶并求用旺；谋文用父、谋利用财、释患用子（占己谋不论应、占彼谋不论世；问成占谋、问吉凶占用）

rule.yi: 所以靠自己的力量能办成的，不用看应；靠别人才能成的事，不用看世。只问成不成，只忌空、冲；兼问吉凶，就要同时求用神旺。谋文书（功名）用父，谋利用财，解除祸患用子。占自己谋的事不论应，占别人谋的事不论世；问成不成看谋（世应、冲空），问吉凶看用（用神）。
rule.en: So for what can be done by one's own strength, one need not look at the Other; for what is done through others, one need not look at the Self. If one asks only whether it comes off, one fears only Void and clash; if one also asks about good and ill, one must also seek the Subject thriving. For documents (a name) use the father line, for profit use Wealth, and for relieving trouble use Output. In divining a scheme of one's own, the Other is not discussed; in divining another's scheme, the Self is not discussed; asking whether it comes off one looks at the scheme (Self, Other, clash, Void), asking about good and ill one looks at the Subject.

zh: 故自力可成，莫观其应，
因人成事，莫观其世。
止问成否，但忌空冲，
兼问吉凶，并求用旺，
谋文用父，谋利用财，释患用子。
yi: 所以靠自己的力量能办成的，不用看应；
靠别人才能成的事，不用看世。
只问成不成，只忌空、冲；
兼问吉凶，就要同时求用神旺。
谋文书用父，谋利用财，解除祸患用子。
en: So for what can be done by one's own strength, one need not look at the Other;
for what is done through others, one need not look at the Self.
If one asks only whether it comes off, one fears only Void and clash;
if one also asks about good and ill, one must also seek the Subject thriving.
For documents use the father line, for profit use Wealth, and for relieving trouble use Output.

zh: 占己谋不论应，占彼谋不论世。
问成占谋，问吉凶占用。
yi: 占自己谋的事不论应，占别人谋的事不论世；
问成不成看谋，问吉凶看用。
en: In divining a scheme of one's own, the Other is not discussed; in divining another's scheme, the Self is not discussed;
asking whether it comes off one looks at the scheme, asking about good and ill one looks at the Subject.

note.yi: 「自力可成」是靠自己的力量能办成的事，不用看应；「因人成事」是靠别人才办成的事，不用看世。「止问成否」是只问成不成，「兼问吉凶」是还要问好坏。「谋文用父」是谋文书、功名用父母，「谋利用财」是谋利用妻财，「释患用子」是解除祸患用子孙（子孙克官鬼）。「用旺」是用神旺相。书里自注：占自己谋的事不论应、占别人谋的事不论世；问成不成看谋（世应、冲空），问吉凶看用（用神）。这一条把『成不成』和『好不好』分成两件事：前者看世应的空冲，后者看用神的旺衰。与易隐谋望占的可否成败（YY.83–YY.85）对着看。
note.en: 'Zili ke cheng' is what can be done by one's own strength, so one need not look at the Other; 'yin ren cheng shi' is what is done only through others, so one need not look at the Self. 'Zhi wen cheng fou' is asking only whether it comes off, and 'jian wen jixiong' is also asking about good and ill. 'For documents use the father line' is using Resource for documents and a name, 'for profit use Wealth' is using the Wealth line, and 'for relieving trouble use Output' is using Output (Output controls Pressure). 'Yong wang' is the Subject thriving. The book's own gloss: in divining a scheme of one's own the Other is not discussed, and in divining another's scheme the Self is not discussed; asking whether it comes off one looks at the scheme (the Self and the Other, clash and Void), and asking about good and ill one looks at the Subject. This entry separates 'whether it comes off' from 'whether it is good' as two things: the first is seen by the Void and clash of the Self and the Other, the second by the strength of the Subject. Read against the question of what can and cannot be done in the Yi Yin on scheming (YY.83-85).

units.title: 营谋·筮嘱托：随所用神（或官、或应、或六亲）皆忌空（空则不力）、忌破（破则无功）、忌六冲克世（疑阻生衅）、随墓助鬼（不利公廷）；旺衰分力之大小、合冲定情之向背、化进勇于事化退倦于行；五行六神断情性不主吉凶

rule.yi: 占嘱托（托人办事），随所取的用神：或者用官，或者用应，或者用六亲，都忌空，空就不出力；都忌破，破就没有功效；都忌六冲克世，那就生疑、受阻、生出嫌隙；随墓、助鬼，就不利于公堂。旺衰来分他出力的大小，合冲来定他情意的向背，化进就勇于办事，化退就倦于行动；五行、六神用来断他的性情，但不要拿它来主断吉凶。金坚直，木从容，水曲折，火燥烈，土诚信；龙和，虎勇，雀再三，武婉转，勾端实，蛇缠绵——这是五行、六神按生旺说的，空、破就反过来。
rule.en: In divining about entrusting a matter to another, one follows the Subject taken: whether Pressure, or the Other, or one of the six relations, all fear Void, and Void means he does not exert himself; all fear broken, and broken means no achievement; all fear a six-clash controlling the Self, which breeds suspicion, obstruction and quarrel; following into the tomb and helping Pressure is unfavourable at the public court. Strength and weakness tell how much force he has; combination and clash fix whether his feeling is toward or against me; changing into an advance means he is bold in the matter, changing into a retreat means he tires of acting; the five phases and the six spirits are used to judge his temper, but one does not make them the master of good and ill. Metal is firm and straight, Wood is easygoing, Water is roundabout, Fire is fierce and hasty, Earth is sincere and faithful; the Azure Dragon is mild, the White Tiger bold, the Vermilion Bird says it again and again, the Dark Tortoise is indirect, Hook Earth is upright and solid, the Coiling Snake clings; this is said of the phases and the six spirits when they are strong, and Void or broken turns it round.

zh: 筮嘱托者，随所用神，
或用官，或用应，或用六亲，
皆忌空，空则不力，
皆忌破，破则无功，
皆忌六冲克世，则疑阻生衅，
随墓助鬼，则不利公廷。
旺衰以分其力之大小，合冲以定其情之向背，
化进则勇于事，化退则倦于行，
五行六神以断其情性，然勿主吉凶也。
yi: 占嘱托的，随所取的用神：
或者用官，或者用应，或者用六亲，
都忌空，空就不出力；
都忌破，破就没有功效；
都忌六冲克世，那就生疑、受阻、生出嫌隙；
随墓、助鬼，就不利于公堂。
旺衰来分他出力的大小，合冲来定他情意的向背，
化进就勇于办事，化退就倦于行动；
五行、六神用来断他的性情，但不要拿它来主断吉凶。
en: In divining about entrusting a matter to another, one follows the Subject taken:
whether Pressure, or the Other, or one of the six relations,
all fear Void, and Void means he does not exert himself;
all fear broken, and broken means no achievement;
all fear a six-clash controlling the Self, which breeds suspicion, obstruction and quarrel;
following into the tomb and helping Pressure is unfavourable at the public court.
Strength and weakness tell how much force he has; combination and clash fix whether his feeling is toward or against me;
changing into an advance means he is bold in the matter, changing into a retreat means he tires of acting;
the five phases and the six spirits are used to judge his temper, but one does not make them the master of good and ill.

zh: 金坚直，木从容，水曲折，火燥烈，土诚信，
龙和，虎勇，雀再三，武婉转，勾端实，蛇缠绵，
此五行六神从生旺言也，空破反之。
yi: 金坚直，木从容，水曲折，火燥烈，土诚信；
龙和，虎勇，雀再三，武婉转，勾端实，蛇缠绵；
这是五行、六神按生旺说的，空、破就反过来。
en: Metal is firm and straight, Wood is easygoing, Water is roundabout, Fire is fierce and hasty, Earth is sincere and faithful;
the Azure Dragon is mild, the White Tiger bold, the Vermilion Bird says it again and again, the Dark Tortoise is indirect, Hook Earth is upright and solid, the Coiling Snake clings;
this is said of the phases and the six spirits when they are strong, and Void or broken turns it round.

note.yi: 「嘱托」是托人办事。「随所用神」是按所托的人取用神：所托的是官，就用官爻；所托的是一般的人，就用应；所托的是亲人，就用相应的六亲。「忌空」「忌破」「忌六冲克世」是对这位受托的人的三个忌；「随墓助鬼，不利公廷」是涉及官司公事时的忌。「化进」「化退」是用神化进、化退（进神、退神，见术语表）。「雀再三」是朱雀反复叮咛、话多；「武婉转」是玄武说话绕弯子；「勾端实」是勾陈端正厚实；「蛇缠绵」是螣蛇缠缠绵绵；「龙和」是青龙温和，「虎勇」是白虎勇悍。书里自注：这些性情是按五行、六神生旺来说的，空、破时反过来。「然勿主吉凶也」是五行六神只断性情，吉凶不由它定，由生克旺衰定。与易林补遗仗托人力（EL.134–137）对着看，那边也是应爻为主、嫌空冲破。
note.en: 'Zhutuo' is entrusting a matter to another. 'Following the Subject taken' is taking the Subject according to whom the matter is entrusted to: if it is an official, the Pressure line is used; if an ordinary person, the Other; if a relative, the corresponding one of the six relations. 'Fears Void', 'fears broken' and 'fears a six-clash controlling the Self' are the three taboos concerning the person who is entrusted; 'following into the tomb and helping Pressure is unfavourable at the public court' is the taboo when a lawsuit or public business is involved. 'Changing into an advance' and 'changing into a retreat' are the Subject changing into an Advancing or Retreating spirit (see the glossary). 'The Vermilion Bird says it again and again' is the Vermilion Bird urging repeatedly and saying much; 'the Dark Tortoise is indirect' is the Dark Tortoise speaking in roundabout ways; 'Hook Earth is upright and solid' is Hook Earth being straight and substantial; 'the Coiling Snake clings' is the Coiling Snake clinging on; 'the Azure Dragon is mild' is the Azure Dragon gentle, and 'the White Tiger is bold' is the White Tiger brave and fierce. The book's own gloss: these natures are said of the phases and six spirits when strong, and when Void or broken it is the other way round. 'But do not make them master good and ill' is that the phases and the six spirits judge only temper, and good and ill are not fixed by them but by generation, control, strength and weakness. Read against the Yilin Buyi on relying on others' help (EL.134-137), where the Other line is also the master and Void, clash and broken are feared.

units.title: 营谋·来去、求己求人与谋之主：谋事之来者谋望并求用神、谋事之去者谋望而不求用神；求于己者世、求于人者应；有交忌冲、无交不忌冲；官鬼乃谋之主俱不可失

rule.yi: 凡是谋事要「来」的（要得到什么），办法是谋望，再同时求用神；谋事要「去」的（要摆脱什么），办法是谋望而不求用神。求于自己的看世，求于别人的看应；有交接的忌冲，没有交接的不忌冲；只有官鬼是谋事的主，都不可失去。
rule.en: For a scheme in which something is to 'come' (something is to be gained), the method is the scheme and hope, and also seeking the Subject; for a scheme in which something is to 'go' (something is to be shaken off), the method is the scheme and hope without seeking the Subject. What is sought from oneself is seen by the Self, what is sought from others by the Other; where there is a meeting, clash is feared, and where there is no meeting, clash is not feared; only Pressure is the master of the scheme, and neither may be lost.

zh: 盖凡谋事之来者，法以谋望而并求用神，
谋事之去者，法以谋望而不求用神。
求于己者世，求于人者应，
有交忌冲，无交不忌冲，
惟官鬼乃谋之主也，俱不可失焉。
yi: 凡是谋事要「来」的，办法是谋望，再同时求用神；
谋事要「去」的，办法是谋望而不求用神。
求于自己的看世，求于别人的看应；
有交接的忌冲，没有交接的不忌冲；
只有官鬼是谋事的主，都不可失去。
en: For a scheme in which something is to 'come', the method is the scheme and hope, and also seeking the Subject;
for a scheme in which something is to 'go', the method is the scheme and hope without seeking the Subject.
What is sought from oneself is seen by the Self, what is sought from others by the Other;
where there is a meeting, clash is feared, and where there is no meeting, clash is not feared;
only Pressure is the master of the scheme, and neither may be lost.

note.yi: 「谋事之来者」按文意是要得到点什么（来我这边）的谋事，「谋事之去者」是要摆脱、除去点什么（从我这边去）的谋事，后者像「释患」那样，不求用神。「谋望」就是谋求和盼望（见易隐谋望占 YY.82）。「有交」是事情需要和对方交接、会面、合作，冲就把交接冲散，所以忌；「无交」是不需要交接，冲就无关紧要。「官鬼乃谋之主」是官鬼在谋事里是主持的一方（掌权、批准的人），所以不能失去。这一条与 YM.85 的「官鬼失而谋无主」是同一个意思。
note.en: 'A scheme that comes' is by the sense a scheme to gain something (to come to my side), and 'a scheme that goes' is a scheme to shake off or get rid of something (to go from my side), the latter being like relieving trouble, where the Subject is not sought. 'Mouwang' is scheming and hoping (see the Yi Yin on scheming and hope, YY.82). 'Where there is a meeting' is a matter that needs meeting, joining or co-operating with the other side, where a clash scatters the meeting and so is feared; 'where there is no meeting' is where no meeting is needed, and a clash is of no consequence. 'Pressure is the master of the scheme' is that in a scheme Pressure is the side that presides (the one who holds power and approves), so it must not be lost. This entry says the same as 'with Pressure lost, the scheme has no master' in YM.85.

units.title: 营谋·嘱托的体与用：专问嘱托重体、专问所谋重用，问嘱托而兼求用神者体用两全事无不吉；嘱托体病虽用得位无成；本占为得不可贰

rule.yi: 凡是专问嘱托的，重体；专问所谋的事的，重用；问嘱托而又兼求用神的，体用两全，事情没有不吉的。然而嘱托的体有病，即使用神得位也不成。所以以眼前这一占为得，不可有二心。
rule.en: When one asks only about the entrusting, the body counts for most; when one asks only about the matter schemed for, the use counts for most; when one asks about the entrusting and also seeks the Subject, with body and use both whole, there is no matter that is not auspicious. But if the body of the entrusting is sick, even if the Subject is well placed it does not come off. So the divination at hand is what is to be taken, and one must not be of two minds.

zh: 盖凡专问嘱托则重体，专问所谋则重用，
问嘱托而兼求用神者，体用两全，事无不吉。
然嘱托体病，虽用得位无成。
故本占为得，不可贰也。
yi: 凡是专问嘱托的，重体；专问所谋的事的，重用；
问嘱托而又兼求用神的，体用两全，事情没有不吉的。
然而嘱托的体有病，即使用神得位也不成。
所以以眼前这一占为得，不可有二心。
en: When one asks only about the entrusting, the body counts for most; when one asks only about the matter schemed for, the use counts for most;
when one asks about the entrusting and also seeks the Subject, with body and use both whole, there is no matter that is not auspicious.
But if the body of the entrusting is sick, even if the Subject is well placed it does not come off.
So the divination at hand is what is to be taken, and one must not be of two minds.

note.yi: 「体」是受托的这个人所对应的爻（他肯不肯出力），「用」是所谋的这件事的用神（谋文用父、谋利用财等，见 YM.86）。「专问嘱托则重体」是只问托人这件事，看托的那个人；「专问所谋则重用」是只问事情本身，看用神；两样都问，就体用两全才吉。「嘱托体病，虽用得位无成」是托的人有病（空、破、克世等），事情的用神再好也成不了：人靠不住，事就落空。「本占为得，不可贰」是以所占的这一件为准，不要同时拿两件事去凑。
note.en: The 'body' is the line that corresponds to the person entrusted (whether he is willing to exert himself), and the 'use' is the Subject of the matter schemed for (documents by the father line, profit by Wealth, and so on, see YM.86). 'Asking only about the entrusting counts the body' is asking only the matter of entrusting someone, looking at the person entrusted; 'asking only about the matter schemed for counts the use' is asking only about the matter itself, looking at the Subject; if both are asked, it is auspicious only when body and use are both whole. 'If the body of the entrusting is sick, even if the Subject is well placed it does not come off' is that if the person entrusted is ailing (Void, broken, controlling the Self and so on), however good the Subject of the matter, it cannot come off: if the man cannot be relied on, the matter comes to nothing. 'The divination at hand is what is to be taken, and one must not be of two minds' is to go by the one matter divined and not to piece two matters together at once.
